title: Play probe snapshot
description: What a built game reports about itself while it runs, so it can be played and judged from outside: `window.__wgf__.play.snapshot()` returns one object of this shape. The game installs it (the template installs `window.__wgf__`; the game adds `play`). It is read-only: calling it never changes the game. The playability step drives the game with real input and reads a snapshot before and after each input; it never acts through the probe. Metric names are the ones the design's `build_spec.experience` and `hud[].metric` use, so a snapshot can be held to the design. `oracle` is present only when the page URL carries `wgf-probe=1`: a shipped build never computes it, and a release refuses a build that would.

state.description: The session state, in these words whatever the game calls them. `won` and `lost` are the ends of play the experience contract names; a result screen after either keeps reporting it until play starts again.

metrics.description: Every metric the design's experience contract relies on (the goal's, win's, lose's, and every metric an action updates), by the same name, at its current value.

entities.description: The things on screen a player must be able to see, with where they are drawn now.

inputs.description: Every input the player can make right now, each as the control action it performs and the real input that performs it.

assets_loaded.description: Runtime asset ids (public/assets/assets.json) the game has loaded so far.

oracle.description: Only with `wgf-probe=1` in the URL: the input that succeeds now (a save, a match, a dodge), or null when no input matters now. Lets the playability step reach `won` and play badly on purpose to reach `lost`.

role.description: What the entity is to the player. The visual gate requires every player, threat, goal, target and projectile entity to be on screen and large enough to read.

x.description: Left edge of its drawn bounds, CSS px from the viewport's left.

y.description: Top edge, CSS px from the viewport's top.

visible.description: Drawn this frame: not hidden, culled, fully transparent or behind another opaque object.

asset.description: The runtime asset id (public/assets/assets.json) that draws it; null when nothing from the manifest does.

render.description: How it is drawn: from a manifest asset, as an engine primitive (a box, sphere, capsule, plain rectangle or circle), as text, or as several assets together. A greybox draws primitives; production draws readable entities from assets unless the design's visual_identity.primitive_style says otherwise.

x.description: CSS px from the viewport's left.

hold_ms.description: How long the input is held down: for a control that acts while held (steer, charge). Absent: a tap or a key press.

key.description: A KeyboardEvent.key value, e.g. ArrowLeft or ' '.
